name: King of Shimron
overview: The King of Shimron was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. He is specifically mentioned in the context of the military campaigns led by Joshua as noted in Joshua 11:1 and 12:20.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Shimron' directly refers to his rulership over the city or region of Shimron. The name means simply 'king of Shimron,' indicating his position rather than a personal name. This title is not given by God but is a descriptive designation in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Shimron beyond what is noted in his title and role among the defeated kings. No additional relational information is provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Shimron is significant as one of the local Canaanite kings who opposed Israel's divinely commanded conquest under Joshua. His defeat represents the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel the land and demonstrates the Lord’s power in delivering victory over the enemies of His people. The mention of his defeat among thirty-one kings underscores the comprehensive nature of Joshua’s campaign.
